content.value_statement: Lark contact workflows often need a safe way to identify the right person before messaging or scheduling. This skill resolves users and profile fields through lark-cli contact commands.
actual_capabilities: Search Lark users by name, email, phone number, or known contact identifiers.
Resolve open IDs for later messaging, scheduling, or profile lookup workflows.
Fetch basic profile details by open ID, union ID, or user ID where supported.
Batch validate up to 100 open IDs and include the current user alias.
Filter users by chat history, enterprise email, tenant boundary, and organization status.
Guide personal status and signature checks through the documented profile query path.
limitations: It does not traverse department trees, list department members, or build organization charts.
Lark visibility rules can hide fields for cross-tenant or restricted users.
The search command requires user identity, while bot get-user requires an explicit user ID.
Search results are not automatically paginated and may need query refinement.

use_cases.title: Find the right colleague
use_cases.description: Resolve a coworker by name or email before sending a message or scheduling a meeting.

use_cases.title: Validate contact records
use_cases.description: Check known open IDs and fill missing names, departments, emails, and activation states.

use_cases.title: Prepare safe handoffs
use_cases.description: Present multiple matching users for confirmation before any follow-up action with side effects.
use_cases.target_user: Support agents and workplace automation builders

prompt_templates.title: Find a coworker
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup by name or email.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Lark open ID for Alice Chen by name. Show likely matches and explain how to choose the right person.

prompt_templates.title: Verify one profile
prompt_templates.scenario: Profile lookup from a known identifier.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Lark open ID to look up the user profile. Return name, department, enterprise email, and any missing fields.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate these Lark open IDs and summarize each person. Include name, department, email, activation status, and tenant status.

prompt_templates.title: Disambiguate before action
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced search before a meeting invite or message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for Wang in Lark, filter to same-tenant users with enterprise email, and prepare candidates. Do not choose a match without confirmation.

output_examples.input: Find Alice Chen by enterprise email before I send a message.
output_examples.output: One likely match is Alice Chen in Sales. The result includes her Lark open ID and enterprise email for confirmation.

output_examples.input: Check these three contact IDs and tell me which users are active.
output_examples.output: The report lists each matching user, activation status, department, and missing fields. One ID resolves to the current user.

output_examples.input: Search for Wang from the same tenant with enterprise email.
output_examples.output: Several candidates match. The safest next step is to ask the user to select the correct person.

best_practices: Ask the user to confirm a person when search returns multiple similar names.
Use enterprise email, department, and recent chat hints to narrow ambiguous results.
Keep lookups within legitimate work needs and the caller's Lark visibility scope.
anti_patterns: Do not select the first matching user for messages, meetings, or other side effects.
Do not use this skill for department trees, department member lists, or organization charts.
Do not treat empty cross-tenant fields as command failures without checking visibility limits.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps resolve Lark contact identities and profile fields through lark-cli contact commands.

faq.question: Does it send messages?
faq.answer: No. It can find contact identifiers, then another Lark messaging skill should send messages.

faq.question: Can it list a department?
faq.answer: No. Department trees and member lists are outside this skill and require native OpenAPI workflows.

faq.question: Which identifiers are supported?
faq.answer: Open ID is the default. Bot get-user can use union ID or user ID when requested.

faq.question: Why are some profile fields empty?
faq.answer: Lark permissions and tenant boundaries can hide email, department, status, or other profile fields.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The generated metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
